applicable_when: The kernel is a GEMM (M=640, N=1152, K=192) with ALLOW_TF32=False, forcing scalar FP32 FFMA instructions instead of Tensor Core MMA. On H200 SXM5, FP32 Tensor Cores deliver 989 TFLOPS vs 67 TFLOPS for scalar FP32 — a ~14.7x theoretical throughput advantage. The FMA pipeline is only at 25.4% utilization, confirming the kernel is not saturating compute. With K=192 (well below the 512 threshold where TF32 mantissa truncation becomes problematic), enabling TF32 is safe for this workload. Additionally, 168 registers/thread is extremely high, capping theoretical occupancy at 18.75% and achieved at just 6.25%. Enabling TF32 allows the compiler to emit MMA instructions which are more register-efficient than the scalar FFMA loop, potentially reducing register pressure and improving occupancy.
